The workspace is a place to read research notes, inspect supporting evidence,
and review a paper as it develops. This page shows the shared reading surface
in light and dark, including headings, links, tables, code and callouts.

## A familiar reading surface

Light mode uses a cream background with dark-teal text. Dark mode uses an
extra-dark teal background with cream text. Both come from
[Asta's design system](https://github.com/allenai/design/tree/main/asta), and both
use the same Manrope type and page layout. Changing the mode keeps the text in
the same place, so you can keep reading where you left off.

The page opens in dark mode on a fresh visit, regardless of your system setting. Use the light/dark
toggle in the navigation to choose a mode yourself. Your choice persists as
you move between pages or reload the site.

::: {.callout-note}
## Keep your place

Scroll through this section. Its heading stays above the text until the next
section takes over. The table of contents also marks the section you are
reading, and its links let you return to a heading directly.
:::

### Reading the components

Links use Asta's teal on the light surface and green on the dark surface.
Inline code such as `asta workspace sync` uses a monospace face. A separate
code block keeps commands easy to scan:

```bash
asta workspace sync
make check
make preview
```

| Part of the page | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Section heading | Keep the current reading context in view |
| Table of contents | Jump to another part of a long page |
| Theme toggle | Choose the light or dark reading surface |
| Evidence highlight | Inspect the quote backing a research claim |

Read the [sample literature review](lit-review/index.qmd) to try an evidence
highlight. Hover over its marked claim, or focus it with the keyboard, to see
the source quote alongside its citation.

[Read the sample review](lit-review/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## A project can choose its own appearance

The theme is a managed workspace asset. A project receives it from the same
selected source as its shared build rules and evidence extension. A refresh
updates those assets together instead of leaving a copied stylesheet behind.

Existing projects adopt the Asta theme when their HTML theme still has the
scaffold's original `cosmo` value and their selected source supplies the new
assets. A project with another theme keeps its choice. Older pinned sources
keep their original appearance until the project selects a compatible release.

### Customize deliberately

For a different HTML theme, edit the project's `_quarto.yml`. Keep any
project-specific styles alongside it:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: flatly
    css: styles.css
```

To customize the Asta theme directly, commit a copy of
`_extensions/asta-theme`. Managed refreshes preserve committed copies and local
development symlinks. This keeps intentional project styling under the
project's own version control.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Share the rendered work

A workspace preview includes the same light/dark controls as the published
site. Send a reader the preview URL so they can inspect the actual page,
follow its links, and choose the reading surface they prefer.
:::
